related_questions.question: How long does the flu virus last?

text_blocks.snippet: The flu virus typically lasts for 3 to 7 days in most people, with fever usually subsiding within 3 to 4 days. However, some symptoms like cough and fatigue can linger for up to two weeks. While the most severe symptoms tend to resolve within 2-3 days, complete recovery can take up to two weeks.

list.snippet: Contagious period: Individuals are contagious from about a day before symptoms appear until 5-7 days after they start. Children and those with weakened immune systems may be contagious for longer.
Fever: Typically lasts 3 to 4 days, but can last up to 8.
Other symptoms: Other symptoms like aches, chills, and fatigue generally improve within 7 to 14 days.
Cough and fatigue: These can persist for up to two weeks, even after other symptoms have subsided.
Full recovery: Most people fully recover within two weeks.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to rest, stay hydrated, and consider over-the-counter medications to manage symptoms during this period. If symptoms worsen or last longer than a week, it's recommended to seek medical advice.

text_blocks.snippet: The flu virus, or influenza virus, is a contagious respiratory illness that can cause mild to severe symptoms, including fever, body aches, and cough. It's spread through respiratory droplets produced when an infected person coughs or sneezes, or by touching contaminated surfaces. While most people recover within a couple of weeks, the flu can be serious, especially for vulnerable groups like young children, older adults, and those with chronic conditions.
snippet_highlighted_words: a contagious respiratory illness that can cause mild to severe symptoms, including fever, body aches, and cough

text_blocks.snippet: Key aspects of the flu virus:

list.title: Types:
list.snippet: The main types of flu viruses that infect humans are influenza A and B. Influenza A viruses are further classified into subtypes based on surface proteins called hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA).

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Common symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, runny or stuffy nose, body aches, headache, and fatigue. Some people, especially children, may also experience vomiting and diarrhea.

list.title: Transmission:
list.snippet: Flu viruses spread easily through respiratory droplets produced when an infected person coughs, sneezes, or talks. It can also be spread by touching contaminated surfaces and then touching your face.

list.title: Contagious Period:
list.snippet: Individuals are typically contagious 24 hours before symptoms appear and remain contagious for up to five to seven days after symptoms start. Children may be contagious for a longer period.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Antibiotics are not effective against the flu, as it is a viral infection. Antiviral medications, if started early, can help shorten the duration and severity of the illness. Over-the-counter pain relievers and decongestants can help manage symptoms.

list.title: Prevention:
list.snippet: Vaccination is the best way to prevent the flu. Practicing good hygiene, such as frequent handwashing and covering coughs and sneezes, can also help reduce the spread of the virus.

list.title: Severity:
list.snippet: While most people recover from the flu without complications, it can be severe, especially for vulnerable populations, leading to hospitalization or even death.

list.title: Diagnosis:
list.snippet: A healthcare provider can diagnose the flu through a medical history, symptom assessment, and potentially a rapid flu test or laboratory testing of a nasal or throat swab.
